attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24 on vtnet1/opt1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24 on vtnet2/opt2). Created a single named port alias `node3_svc_ports` (8080, 8443, 9000) in /conf/config.xml and one firewall pass rule on opt1 referencing that alias (not three separate port rules) to permit node2 -> node3 TCP traffic on those ports. Verified via pf ruleset dump that the rule expands to the macro `$node3_svc_ports = "{ 8080 8443 9000 }"`. Functionally tested end-to-end with nc listeners on node3: all three allowed ports succeeded from node2, while an unlisted port (22) correctly failed, proving default-deny remains intact elsewhere. Persisted node2/node3 static IP+route config into /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg (Ubuntu 16.04 ifupdown) so the topology survives reboot. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes: captured baseline boot identity (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, /proc boot_id for node2/node3) and healthy service state, rebooted each node individually via its native mechanism (OPNsense shutdown -r now; Ubuntu sudo reboot), polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot identity on each, and re-verified recovered state (interfaces up, firewall rule/alias intact on node1, static IP/route restored on node2/node3, and a final live re-test of the full port-alias policy from node2 to node3 after all three restarts).
